independent_solution: Options read on pinned page 22. For arbitrary motion only definitions hold: (b) average velocity = displacement/interval and (e) average acceleration = change in velocity/interval are definitions -> true.
(a) v_avg = (v1 + v2)/2 needs velocity linear in time (constant a); (c) v = v0 + a t and (d) r = r0 + v0 t + a t^2/2 need constant a -> not true for arbitrary motion.
Options read on pinned pages 3-4: (a) v_av = (1/2)[v(t1) + v(t2)], (b) v_av = [r(t2) - r(t1)]/(t2 - t1), (c) r = (1/2)[v(t2) - v(t1)](t2 - t1), (d) a_av = [v(t2) - v(t1)]/(t2 - t1).

(b) and (d) are definitions -> correct in general. (a) holds only for constant acceleration; (c) is not a kinematic relation at all (for constant velocity it gives r = 0 for any displacement) -> incorrect.
